enable_reasoning.description: Opt in to chain-of-thought / reasoning emission on reasoning models (Nemotron-V3, DeepSeek-R1). Default False because reasoning eats max_tokens budget; truncation strands the answer mid-<think>. Set True only for judge-style workers that want the reasoning trace in response_message.reasoning_content.
enable_reasoning.title: Enable Reasoning

frequency_penalty.description: OpenAI-standard frequency penalty. Forwarded verbatim to OpenAI-compatible upstreams when set, omitted when None. Not sent to Anthropic. Recorded in the ``inference_call`` ledger.
frequency_penalty.title: Frequency Penalty

max_tokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate in the response. Accepts the OpenAI-modern `max_completion_tokens` alias because pydantic-ai 1.x and openai-python 2.x both serialise the field under that name; without the alias the field arrived as None and vLLM defaulted to `max_model_len - prompt` (~8000), which blew past IR's 600s ReadTimeout on every structured-output call and tripped the breaker (2026-05-19 trust.pdf incident). Capped at 16384 as a hard ceiling: on 2026-05-13 an uncapped request from WM let vLLM (Nemotron-3 on SM120/GB10) fill the remaining ~130k tokens of its 131k context window and crashed in a CUTLASS TMA-WS FP4-MoE kernel. This bound is the last line of defense — callers that send oversized values get a clean 422 instead of triggering an engine restart.
max_tokens.title: Max Tokens

ChatMessage.description:
A single chat message in the conversation.

OpenAI's chat-completion spec defines ``content`` as either a plain
string OR a list of typed content parts (``{type: text, text: ...}``,
``{type: image_url, image_url: ...}``) for multimodal input. We
accept both on the request side and pass them through untouched to
the upstream provider — vision-capable models (claude, gpt-4o,
gemini, gemma-4) consume the list form natively.

On the response side, models always emit plain string content, so
response-handling code at use sites narrows with a runtime
isinstance check.

content.description: Message content. Either plain text (string) or a list of OpenAI-compat content parts for multimodal input. May be None on responses from reasoning models that emit only reasoning_content (e.g. Nemotron-V3, DeepSeek-R1) — downstream should fall back to reasoning_content.

post.description: Collapses ``canary_version`` into ``active_version`` and clears all canary state for the worker. The actual prompt swap is performed in worker_management — this endpoint only flips the local routing pointer.
post.summary: Promote a prompt canary to the new active version

post.description:
Writes/updates the ``prompt_canary_routing`` row for *worker_name*. The auto-rollback monitor reads these rows and clears the canary fields if observed metrics breach ``rollback_thresholds``. Re-calling this endpoint within an active window updates the existing row (UPSERT) so the prompt-loop can extend the window or change the split percent without first promoting/aborting.

``rollback_thresholds`` accepts exactly the keys the monitor enforces — ``failure_rate`` (0-1 fraction, 0.05 == 5%), ``p95_latency_ms`` (milliseconds) and ``cost_usd`` (US dollars); each is a max, breached when observed > threshold. Anything else is a 400. NOTE: ``cost_usd`` is accepted but cannot currently breach — canary replies are served by worker_management, which has no priced provider entry, so attributed cost is always 0.0. The monitor logs ``canary_cost_threshold_unenforceable`` when one is configured.
post.summary: Configure (upsert) a K%-split prompt canary window

get.description: Returns the current row for *worker_name*. The QA subflow polls this during the observation window: if ``canary_version`` is NULL when it previously had a value, the auto-rollback monitor cleared it (rollback fired). Returns 404 if no row exists.
get.summary: Read the current prompt_canary_routing state for a worker

post.description: Clears all canary state for the worker, reverting routing to the known-good active_version. Bypasses the autonomous regression monitor — an operator (via fr) triggers this directly. Idempotent: re-calling on an already-cleared row returns the same active_version.
post.summary: Operator-triggered rollback of a prompt canary to the active version

get.description:
How much traffic in the window is pinned (``temperature = 0`` and a seed).

Counts every call in the window, not only ``status = 'ok'`` ones --
pinning is a request property, independent of outcome. ``source`` is the
same filter, with the same NULL-as-``unknown`` handling, as
``repeat-groups``. ``callers`` is ordered by ``n`` descending.

get.description:
Identical requests answered more than once, and whether the answers agree.

``temperature`` is an equality on the stored temperature (rows with a NULL
temperature are excluded once it is given); ``caller``, ``served_provider``
and ``source`` filter calls before grouping. ``seeded=true`` restricts to
calls with a non-NULL ``seed``, ``seeded=false`` to calls with a NULL
``seed``; omitted, no filter. ``summary`` covers every group in the
window, not just the page; groups are ordered disagreeing first, then
newest ``last_at``. Each group reports ``served_models_n`` (see the
``_REPEAT_GROUPS_CTE`` comment for how a NULL served model is counted);
``summary.straddling_groups`` is the count of groups where that is > 1.
See the block comment above for ``source``, ``summary.by_source`` and
``summary.callers``.

get.description:
The captured request/response of one row; 404 if it was not captured.

``request`` is what the ledger stored: ``{"model": ..., **fingerprint}``.
``request_sha256`` hashes the fingerprint WITHOUT ``model``, and
``request_sha256_verified`` says whether re-hashing the stored body (canonical
JSON, sorted keys) reproduces it -- so a consumer freezing a tuple from this
body knows whether it round-tripped JSONB exactly.

``request_text`` / ``response_text`` are the EXACT bytes sent to and
received from the provider (key order preserved; replay these, not
``request``). ``request_text_verified`` says whether sha256(request_text)
equals the stored ``request_text_sha256``; NULL when no text was stored.

get.description:
List available models.

Sourced from the live provider catalog (``app.state.provider_catalog``),
not a hard-coded list, so it never drifts from the deployed ConfigMap:

* A ``default`` entry whose chain is the effective default failover chain
  (catalog ``default_chain`` minus any disabled provider — mirrors the
  ``effective_default_chain`` computed in ``main.py``).
* One entry per model id served by each *enabled* provider (its default
  ``model`` plus its stable aliases, via ``ProviderEntry.model_ids()``),
  pinned to the provider that serves it. This is what makes the abstract
  ``local-llm`` name discoverable here.

TENANT-SCOPED (owner ruling 2026-10-01, ``services.tenant_policy``): for a
CUSTOMER tenant (anything not a platform tenant, including a missing/nil
``X-Tenant-Id``) only providers that tenant may be routed to are listed,
Commercial providers are listed only for a PROVEN commercial-platform
tenant (``TenantPolicy.has_commercial_access``: listed in
``COMMERCIAL_PLATFORM_TENANT_IDS`` AND proven by a verified licence token
on this request): an asserted platform ``X-Tenant-Id`` without proof gets
the customer view.

The tenant is resolved by ``security.require_listing_tenant`` -- the same
introspection + delegation rule the completions route applies -- so a
header completions would not honour cannot buy the platform view here.

Return the catalog providers this tenant may be routed to.

A platform (or commercial-granted) tenant sees the whole catalog; a CUSTOMER
tenant -- including a missing/nil ``X-Tenant-Id`` -- sees only
``customer_eligible`` providers (owner ruling 2026-10-01).

Return the models exposed by a single provider.

Source of truth is the optional ``models`` field on the ProviderEntry.
When that list is empty, the provider's default ``model`` is returned as
the single entry.

patch.description: The replay runner correlates its verdict to an inference via the ``correlation_id`` it issued — it never learns the row's UUID primary key. This endpoint backfills ``expected`` (and optionally ``validation_passed`` / ``judge_score``) on the row carrying that correlation_id, using the ``replay_invocation_log_corr`` index. A 404 surfaces a broken correlation chain loudly. Scoped to the caller's own tenant: another tenant's row is a 404.

patch.description: Replay runners write the row at invocation time but learn the validation outcome later (after schema check + LLM judge). This endpoint backfills ``validation_passed`` and/or ``judge_score`` without re-inserting. Scoped to the caller's own tenant: another tenant's row is a 404.
